children: Accel India sold a 1.84 per cent stake while 360 ONE Group offloaded 2.23 per cent through separate BSE block deals

Venture capital firm Accel India and 360 ONE Group have sold a combined 4.07 per cent stake in omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle for Rs 513 crore through separate block deals on the BSE.
The two investors sold a combined 61.98 lakh shares of Bengaluru-based BlueStone on Thursday, according to exchange data. The transactions were executed at an average price of Rs 827.60 per share.

Accel India, through its affiliate Accel India III (Mauritius) Ltd, sold 28 lakh shares, representing a 1.84 per cent stake. 360 ONE Group, through its funds, offloaded 33.98 lakh shares, or a 2.23 per cent stake.
Following the transaction, Accel’s holding through its affiliates declined to 8.71 per cent from 10.55 per cent.

The shares were acquired by a mix of domestic and overseas institutional investors at the same price. Mutual funds managed by Mirae Asset, Nippon India and Bandhan, along with Bajaj Life Insurance, participated in the transaction.
SBI Life Insurance also acquired more than 9.5 lakh shares, representing a 0.6 per cent stake, for Rs 79 crore. Its holding in BlueStone increased to 5.02 per cent from 4.4 per cent.
Foreign investors participating in the transaction included Goldman Sachs, Citigroup Global Markets Singapore and sovereign wealth fund Kuwait Investment Authority.
BlueStone shares fell 1.48 per cent to Rs 793.10 apiece on the BSE on Friday.

The stake sale follows BlueStone’s financial performance in the April-June quarter. The company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5.96 crore for the first quarter, compared with a net loss of Rs 34.74 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income increased 49 per cent to Rs 751.81 crore, while expenses rose to Rs 744.82 crore from Rs 538.45 crore.
The latest transaction marks the second round of stake sales by the investors this year. In June, Accel, 360 ONE and IvyCap Ventures sold shares of BlueStone for nearly Rs 243 crore.

Founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and Vidya Nataraj, BlueStone operates in the jewellery segment and offers products including rings, pendants and earrings. It competes with brands including Titan’s CaratLane and GIVA.
